_comment: Default proficiency scale. instructions.txt asks for 'a proficiency template that they can edit (default: Entry, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert with proficiency criteria you generate once during build)' — so these generic criteria are authored here as build-time data, not produced by a runtime LLM call. The per-skill-cluster wording IS generated at runtime, using these as the rubric.

levels.name: Entry
levels.criteria: Applies the skill to routine, well-defined situations with guidance available. Follows established methods rather than selecting between them, and escalates anything unfamiliar. Output is checked by others before it is relied upon.
levels.typical_autonomy: Works to instruction with regular review.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.criteria: Applies the skill independently across the range of situations normally encountered in the role. Chooses between established approaches and recognises when a situation falls outside them. Output is generally relied upon without rework.
levels.typical_autonomy: Works independently on familiar problems; seeks input on novel ones.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.criteria: Handles complex, ambiguous or contested situations where established methods are insufficient, and adapts them with sound judgement. Recognised internally as a point of reference, and reviews or guides the work of others.
levels.typical_autonomy: Sets own approach; accountable for judgement calls.

levels.name: Expert
levels.criteria: Shapes how the skill is practised beyond their own work — setting standards, resolving the hardest cases, and building capability in others. Judgement is sought on decisions with significant or organisation-wide consequence.
levels.typical_autonomy: Defines practice; influences direction beyond own remit.
